original_question: Let omega denote a complex nth root of unity such that the ring of numbers a + b omega has unique factorization. Is the configuration of omega-primes symmetric with respect to the regular 2n-gon?
target_in_paper: Unsolved Problem 25: the conjecture about symmetry of the configuration of ω-primes in the ring of numbers a+bω. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it has the same ambient objects (numbers of the form a+bω), the same hypothesis of unique factorization, the same focus on ω-primes, and the same geometric question about symmetry relative to a regular 2n-gon. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper implicitly treats the ambient ring as Z[ω]={a+bω : a,b∈Z}; the integers a and b should be stated explicitly for the question to be stand-alone. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
The paper writes the condition on ω as ω^{n-1}+ω^{n-2}+⋯+1=0; that displayed relation is part of the official statement's setup. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
The nearby context explicitly lists the units as ±1, ±ω, ±ω^2, …, ±ω^{n-1}; your draft omits this. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The phrase 'ω-primes' should be defined explicitly as the prime elements of Z[ω], since the paper uses the term without a separate definition. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The geometric phrase should be unpacked by saying that the configuration is considered after embedding Z[ω] in C, and that 'symmetric of the regular 2n-gon' means invariant under the symmetries of a regular 2n-gon. This clarifies the paper's wording without broadening it. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let ω be a complex n-th root of unity satisfying ω^{n-1}+ω^{n-2}+⋯+1=0, and let Z[ω]={a+bω : a,b∈Z} be assumed to enjoy unique factorization, with units ±1, ±ω, ±ω^2, …, ±ω^{n-1}. Viewing Z[ω] as a subset of C, is the configuration of its prime elements (the ω-primes) invariant under the symmetries of a regular 2n-gon? ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: Unsolved Problem 25 on p. 21 states, after introducing numbers a+bω with unique factorization and listing the units, the conjecture that 'The configuration of ω primes are symmetric of the 2n regular polygon.' The paper gives no separate theorem, proposition, or proved equivalent reformulation for this item, so the faithful refinement is to keep the question narrow and only make explicit the ambient ring, the meaning of ω-primes, and the geometric symmetry language already present there. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
